reading.body:
Covariant is recorded as a for-profit startup, and the available data says nothing about what it builds or operates.

The record contains no products, no cases, and no model context protocol entries. The only substantive fact is the company's own website and its for-profit status. The site text captured amounts to the company name alone, with no description of its work.

That absence matters for an AI infrastructure argument because it leaves the compute question unanswerable here. There is no way to tell from this data whether Covariant trains models, sells software, or consumes power and floor space at all. A company in this dataset cannot be placed on the compute-to-buildings-to-power chain without facts that are not present.

What the data does not cover is nearly everything. It does not say what Covariant makes, where it operates, how much compute it uses, or what legal or regulatory exposure it carries. It should be read as a stub record, not as evidence about the company's role in AI scaling.
